question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 7 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{34}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{34}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 7 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 & -3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 & -3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+4}|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
